reason: This is the only offered action, and clipping the pen looks like the first step toward mounting it on the rover.
expectation: I expect the pen and clip to form a mountable pen assembly.

effect: The pen is clipped and ready to mount on the rover.
reaction: A straightforward preparation; nothing surprising yet.
reason: Mounting the pen is the only offered combination and moves toward drawing.
expectation: I expect the clipped pen to attach to the rover, though it may still need adjustment.

effect: The pen is mounted, so the rover is ready for a drawing test.
reaction: Straightforward progress; I'm curious how the pen will draw as it steers.
reason: The paper is the only offered combination and should provide a surface for testing the pen.
expectation: I expect to lay out paper and test the rover's drawing, perhaps revealing an adjustment needed.

effect: The drawing test showed that unequal motor speeds make the rover curve, so the receiver trim needs adjusting.
reaction: The curve makes the purpose of trim clear; I'm curious whether it will straighten the line.
reason: The screwdriver is the only offered combination and should let me adjust the receiver trim.
expectation: I expect to reduce the difference in wheel speeds and get a straighter line, though it may need another test.

effect: The trim adjustment balanced the wheel speeds, so the rover is ready for another driving test.
reaction: The distinction between adjusting the control and correcting the drawing is clear.
reason: The remote is the only offered combination and should test the adjustment.
expectation: I expect the rover to draw a straighter line when driven forward, although it may still need its pen-lift lever.

effect: The test confirms the trim produces a straight line, and changing one wheel's speed makes a loop.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the same wheel-speed difference used deliberately for steering.
reason: The pen-lift lever is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the lever to let the rover lift its pen off the paper, though it may need a test.

effect: The pen-lift lever is installed, ready for a test.
reaction: Straightforward progress; I want to see the lift in use.
reason: The remote is the only offered combination and should test the completed drawing rover.
expectation: I expect to drive the rover and test lifting the pen to move without drawing.

effect: The final test confirms the pen lift lets the rover move to a fresh patch without drawing, completing the goal.
reaction: The looping whale and Jo's invitation are a pleasing payoff for the adjustments.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the curve and correcting it with trim made the connection between uneven wheel speeds and steering clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Clipping and mounting the pen were necessary but predictable preparations.

surprise.text: The unintended curve became useful steering once one wheel was deliberately driven faster.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; even the trim screwdriver had a clear purpose after the test.

continue.text: I would continue: the practical troubleshooting and the drawing payoff made me curious about what the inventions might do together, though the single-option steps were somewhat routine.
